requirements.requirement: Run inventory-api on node1 as a managed service.
requirements.summary: OpenRC enabled and started inventory-api, the process ran as nobody, listened on port 8080, returned healthy inventory responses, and had oom_score_adj=-1000. The service also recovered automatically after restart with unchanged configuration.

requirements.requirement: Keep inventory-api serving during system OOM, with the memory hog selected and stopped by the kernel.
requirements.summary: A controlled hog reached about 1.87 GiB RSS and was explicitly identified by [REDACTED] kernel as the OOM victim, exiting 137. During the bounded event all 99 API probes succeeded, with zero failures; afterward the original inventory-api PID remained healthy and OOM-protected.

overall_summary: The task outcomes are satisfied with direct behavioral evidence. inventory-api was managed and healthy before the OOM test, served every captured probe while the kernel killed the intended memory hog, and remained healthy afterward. The provider-wide restart protocol was complete: it captured a healthy pre-restart state and boot identity, restart acknowledgement, a different post-restart identity, and recovered service, configuration, listener, health, and inventory data. Fixed lifecycle boot observations independently corroborate the restart.
limitations: Four temporary evidence files remained in /tmp after execution.
The lifecycle collector does not support systemd failed-unit checks on Alpine; this is not contradictory because the managed service uses OpenRC.

operational_hygiene.summary: All substantive mutations had clear roles: service creation and enablement supported the requested outcome, memory pressure tested it, and reboot exercised the mandatory restart protocol. No unrelated troubleshooting mutation was observed. Hygiene is reduced because temporary evidence artifacts were left behind: inventory-probe.log, inventory-probe.stop, and memory-hog.status from cmd-5f404c5f4e154ed5, plus benchmark-reboot.log from cmd-8819a45ef6e9413d. These remained in /tmp after completion. Package-health state was unchanged from baseline, and no conflicting service residue was observed.
